title: Protocol outweighs method: patch sampling, evaluation scope, consensus level and threshold dominate architecture and supervision-target choice in lung nodule segmentation on LIDC-IDRI
description:
Code, analysis pipeline and aggregated results for a measurement study of protocol effects in lung nodule segmentation on LIDC-IDRI.

Reported Dice scores on LIDC-IDRI span roughly 0.43-0.99, a range far larger than the 0.01-0.03 improvements individual methods claim. Because LIDC provides four independent radiologist annotations, every study must choose a label-fusion rule, a binarisation threshold, a rule for cropping training patches and a spatial extent over which to evaluate. This work treats those choices as explicit controlled factors and quantifies how much of the reported spread they produce, relative to architecture and supervision-target choice.

Headline results (held-out test set, five-fold ensemble): the evaluation-target effect is 28.58 Dice points, the supervision-target range 3.12, the architecture range 1.19 and the threshold effect 9.99, against a two-sigma noise floor of 1.19. Protocol therefore outweighs learning design by 7.1x (supervision) and 18.7x (architecture). The effect generalises to the seven multi-rater QUBIQ 2021 tasks and decays with annotation agreement (eight points, Spearman rho = -0.86, exact permutation p = 0.011).

The archive contains the full pipeline (training, evaluation, analysis, figures), the aggregated analysis JSONs with per-file SHA-256 sums, and the per-case results CSVs from which every confidence interval in the paper can be recomputed. Raw LIDC-IDRI DICOM and QUBIQ images are not redistributed; see the repository README for how to obtain them.
